The Design
System

Five accepted parts. The world it happens in, the mode that inverts it, and three figures called on when the work needs a person to make a point.

00 — Foundations

Three layers, one light.

Everything in this system belongs to one of three layers, and the layer decides how a thing behaves — not how it looks.

  • Forge — made

    Dimensional surfaces. Brushed metal, struck relief, real material under real light. Things that were manufactured.

  • Garden — staged

    The constructed world. Built, never found. See 01.

  • Livery — said

    Flat type, hairlines, interface. One colour, no dimension, nothing pretending to be an object.

Bronze appears in all three — as brushed metal, as emitted light, and as flat ink. It is the only value that crosses freely, and that is what makes the three layers read as one brand rather than three.

One raking light, low, from the upper left. Everywhere, in every layer. Two sources is a bug, not a style choice. Specular is a narrow near-white line at #FEFEF5 — never gold, never a bloom around a whole silhouette.

A palette here is a set of materials, not a set of colours. Each value carries a base, a surface behaviour and a light response. Every number in brand/tokens.css was measured off a generated asset and every text pair has a recorded contrast ratio. Nothing was picked off a swatch.

Bronze cannot hold text on paper. So in day mode the role holds and the value swaps: oxide takes bronze's job. Nothing is redrawn, nothing is reversed, no alternate artwork exists.

01 — The Dreamed Garden

Built, never found.

A zen garden as dreamed by an abstract digital artist. The feel of the place, but strange. Calm, but wrong.

Pixel Blade does not show you the buyer's world. It builds a model of that world and walks you through it. Which is what advertising actually is — and it is why the garden is a stage, a gallery or an exhibition, never a location.

Two gamuts. One boundary.

We are in a dark room, looking into a bright world. The frame edge is the wall between them.

  • Interface gamut

    Sumi, graphite, petrol, bronze, washi. Narrow, disciplined, contrast-verified. This is the dark room.

  • Image gamut

    All of the above plus ember, coral, blush, rust, oxide. This is the lit world, and it lives strictly inside imagery.

  • The hard rule

    Saturated warm colour is forbidden in type, tiles, buttons, rules, borders, backgrounds and any text section. Permitted, without limit, inside a picture.

It is not a foreign palette. The warm range lands at hue 12–20, directly adjacent to bronze at hue 29 — the same family, turned up. Bronze is the only value that crosses the boundary in both directions.

The ceiling is coverage, not chroma. ≤25% chroma coverage, ≥50% ground. Peak saturation is explicitly not a failure condition. This is measured, not judged — see 04.

The edge is a falloff.

Enforced by brand/feather.py. Working inset 0.10–0.14.

02 — Daylight Mode

Tech, and the dream it stays inside.

Elegance, engineering, and a dream of what the future could be — deliberately separate from cyber. What does the future look like made into a diorama, textured with anything from wood and steel to construction paper, and made achingly beautiful in three dimensions.

Standing instruction on this term: stay in the dream.

Roles hold. Values swap.

The homepage is dark. A page about shifts in paradigms, or implementation, moves to day — and the site changes gear without changing identity.

Bronze's failure on paper is not a limitation the system works around — it is the mechanism the system is built on. Because bronze cannot appear on a light ground, day mode can never be a tinted version of night. It has to be a genuine gear change.

03 — The Warriors

A separate element. Loaded only when needed.

Not a mode, not a palette, not a term. The Warriors are a cast — called on when the work needs a person to make a point, and silent the rest of the time. Never loaded for ordinary design or layout work.

Saturation is the axis. All three sit in bronze's own hue family — 24–34 — and differ only in volume. The student is over-saturated; he is trying too hard. The master has worn it below the brand's own level. Mastery is turning it down — which is the same argument the agency makes about advertising.

FigureHueSaturationReading
Samurai — the student24–2963–79Louder than the brand
Bronze — the brand2959The brand itself
Monk — the master28–345–45Quieter than the brand

Three rendering modes, on purpose. Monk is photoreal cloth. Samurai is photoreal, then ink. Ninja is cel-shaded anime, then pixels. The only constant is the dissolution. Unifying the technique would flatten three distinct figures into one.

No adversary. The Oni is struck from the roster — no enemy is shown on the site. Revisit only when video assets are in play.

The Monk — final form

No longer hiding from the sun. Watercolour and mist and motion — in motion simply by standing still.

He is made of the brand. His cloth quantizes to #624B37 · #9D8671 · #C2946B · #CEAF91 · #E0D3C2 · #F1EFE6 — every one at hue 28–34, against bronze at 29. He is the bronze family worn down, which is why he never looks composited into these environments.

He crosses both modes without adaptation, and the reason is measurable rather than aesthetic: his wardrobe spans the full value range. On sumi his light layers carry him at up to 17.18:1; on paper his shadow layers do at 7.44:1. He contains both ends, so he needs no day version.

The Samurai — the Day warrior

Inky, shadowed. The hat hides him from a sun he is not yet worthy of receiving. He is learning to dance, but carries too much shadow.

Where he is solid, he is a photograph. Where he is not, he is a brush stroke. The dissolution only carries weight because what remains is photographically real — if everything is ink, nothing is lost.

Always the hat. The face is always shadowed. Bursts of colour sit behind his weapon — a glimpse of what he might become once he is done learning. The dissolution is the only stylised element in the image.

The Ninja

Shinji Aramaki anime in texture, movement and execution. Warriors that might be myth — until you get back to your hideout, and everyone is dead.

The stillness is the threat. He is not the hero of the scene, he is the thing that already happened. No action poses, no crescendo, no confrontation. Aftermath is rendered with no bodies, no damage and no gore — only dust, emptiness and him.

Settings are future Tokyo. A cybernetic limb is permitted. Brighter values from the palette are preferred, and new ones may be added as needed.

04 — Enforcement

Every measurable rule is a tool.

Rules that live only in a document drift. These are executable, so a plate either passes or it does not — and three scope bugs in the gate were found by new kinds of image rather than by anyone reading the spec.

  • check-plate.py

    The gate. [--day] [--figure] <image>… Fails on chroma coverage and on edge seam. Never fails on saturation. Run it on everything.

  • feather.py

    Vignettes a plate into the page ground so the boundary is a falloff, not a line. [--day], working inset 0.10–0.14.

  • pixelate.py

    The Ninja's dissolve. Blocks grow as they travel, and a loose block is redrawn at the size of where it lands, not where it came from.

  • tokens.css

    The authority. Every value measured off a generated asset, every text pair with a recorded ratio.

CheckThreshold
Chroma coverage≤ 25%
Ground, standard plate≥ 50%
Ground, Warrior portrait≥ 35%
Edge delta to page ground≤ 12
Peak saturationUnbounded — by design

05 — Not yet settled

What this system does not have.

Stated plainly so nobody builds on something that was never agreed.

  • The mark open

    Five rounds proposed, five rejected. Nothing in the repo's marks/, mark/ or forms/ directories is part of this system. They are kept as a record of what has already failed.

  • Typography unargued

    Bodoni Moda, Archivo 300 and JetBrains Mono are a round-one proposal that has never been defended. The oldest unexamined thing here.

  • Components absent

    No button, nav or card specification beyond a single hero comp.

  • Motion absent

    No spec, despite parallax, pixel dissolve and day↔night all being implied by the above.

  • The aperture homeless

    A ring that stops containing and becomes a hole, with a world behind the page. The strongest single idea to come out of the reference work, and it has no home yet. Likely a site device rather than a mark.

  • Site design deferred

    The layered, three-dimensional feel of moving through an environment. Phase three.
